title: A Pop-Up Says My Computer Has a Virus!
youtube_title: Fake Virus Pop-Up? What to Do (and Never Do) | Fix It Friday
next: Next Friday: another fix from your comments
description: A loud warning fills your screen: your computer is infected, call this number now. Kip and Bub explain why it's fake, how to close it safely, and what to do if you already called or let someone into your computer, including the follow-up call that tells you to move your money.

scenes.say: Suddenly your screen goes red. An alarm beeps. It says your computer is infected, and you must call this number right now. What do you do?
It's Fix It Friday. Today: a pop-up says my computer has a virus!
Here's the good news. That warning is fake. It's just a web page made to look scary. Real companies like Microsoft and Apple don't put phone numbers in warnings like that.
The tricks are always the same. A loud alarm, a scary countdown, a company logo, and a phone number to call right now.
If you call, a friendly person says they'll fix it. They ask to get into your computer, then charge you hundreds of dollars for repairs you never needed.
So here's the fix. Don't call the number, and don't click anything inside the warning. Just close your web browser.
Won't close? Restart the computer. Hold the power button until it turns off, wait a moment, then turn it back on. If your browser offers to restore your pages, choose No.

Already called, or let them in? Turn off the internet, run a virus scan with Windows Security or your security app, and change your passwords. Call your bank or card company about any charges, and report it at ReportFraud dot F T C dot gov.

Then watch for the next call. Someone may say they're from your bank or the government, and that you must move your money to a safe account. That's the same scam. Hang up, and call your bank's real number yourself.

card.text: Never move money to a "safe" account.
card.sub: Hang up and call your bank yourself

scenes.say: So: the warning is fake. Don't call, close the browser, and restart if you need to.
Share this with someone who'd panic at that alarm. Got a tech problem you want fixed? Leave it in the comments. See you next Friday.
